template.name: discovery
template.source: Structure of a discovery hub AHEAD has delivered.

cover.title: {client} {engagement}: {phase} Discovery Findings
cover.lede: What {phase} found across {client}'s current estate, what it means for the target architecture, and what {next_phase} should design.

blocks.guide: The overarching finding of {phase} in two or three sentences, written as a conclusion rather than a description of the work. This is the message the readout opens with.

items.title: What it means for the architecture
items.guide: The one or two architectural consequences of the headline finding, stated as direction rather than design.

items.title: What {next_phase} should focus on
items.guide: Where {next_phase} should concentrate its design effort, and why.

blocks.guide: The five to seven findings that matter most, one sentence each, each traceable to the register or to a named session, document or test.

sections.title: Evidence behind the findings
sections.intro: Every finding in this hub rests on one or more of these evidence streams.

items.title: Key sessions with {client}
items.guide: The workshops and deep dives held, who from {client} took part (by role), and what each covered.

items.title: Documentation and artefact review
items.guide: The documents, diagrams and repositories reviewed, and what they were used to confirm.

items.title: Architecture review
items.guide: How the delivery team's architects tested and challenged the emerging hypotheses.

items.title: Feasibility testing
items.guide: The hands-on tests run, and what they were designed to prove or disprove.

sections.title: Deliverables and where to find them

blocks.guide: One row per contracted deliverable, named exactly as in the SOW, with the tab that contains it.

sections.title: Key terms used in this hub

blocks.guide: Definitions of the terms and acronyms used across the hub.

tabs.label: Hypothesis and Decision Register
tabs.title: Hypothesis and Decision Register
tabs.question: Every hypothesis tested, decision recorded and experiment run, with the evidence behind it and what it means for {next_phase}.

hero.title: Hypotheses, decisions and experiments
hero.lede: Every hypothesis tested, decision recorded and experiment run in {phase}, with the evidence behind it and what it means for {next_phase}.

blocks.guide: How items are identified, prioritized and given a status. Keep High priority for the few items that shape the architecture.
The register is generated from the config items or a CSV/XLSX file (items_file). Each item needs an ID, type, title, statement, priority, status, area, evidence and next step.

tabs.label: Current-State Estate
tabs.title: Current-State Estate
tabs.question: What {client} runs today, who uses it and how, and what the current estate tells us.

hero.title: {client}'s current estate
hero.lede: What {client} runs today, who uses it and how. This tab describes the current state only; direction is set out on the Architecture Hypothesis tab.

sections.title: What the current estate tells us

blocks.guide: Three to five observations about the estate as a whole, each with the evidence behind it.
One row per platform or shared capability in scope.
The user groups, projects and workflows the estate serves, and how their needs differ.
Representative implementations and workflows, described as they work today.
What could not be seen or confirmed in {phase}, and how that affects confidence in the findings.

tabs.label: Maturity Assessment
tabs.title: Maturity Assessment
tabs.question: How mature each platform is in design and in implementation, dimension by dimension.

hero.title: Design and implementation maturity
hero.lede: How mature each platform is, scored dimension by dimension against a common rubric.

blocks.guide: The headline pattern across the estate, and how scoring works: who scored, against what evidence, and how design and implementation differ.
Scores per platform (rows) and dimension (columns), generated from the config. Add a note per cell to explain each score.
The patterns the heatmap reveals and the action each one implies for {next_phase}.
Confirm the rubric with the team before scoring.
rows: In place for some teams or platforms, not yet consistent.
Measured, monitored and improved over time.

tabs.label: Control Assessment
tabs.title: Control and Governance Assessment
tabs.question: Where controls and governance hold across the estate, and where they lose consistency.

hero.title: Control and governance posture
hero.lede: Where controls hold across the estate, and where they lose consistency.

blocks.guide: The headline finding on controls and governance, and the pattern across the estate.
Scores per platform (rows) and control domain (columns), generated from the config.

sections.title: Control domains: evidence behind the scores

blocks.guide: One row per control domain.
One row per open control question.

tabs.label: Architecture Hypothesis
tabs.title: Architecture Hypothesis
tabs.question: The requirements the future architecture must meet, the current-state architecture, and the hypothesis {next_phase} will design against.

hero.title: Architecture hypothesis
hero.lede: The requirements the future architecture must meet, the current-state architecture, and the hypothesis {next_phase} will design against. This is a hypothesis, not a design.

blocks.guide: The requirements the future architecture must satisfy, each a short title and one or two sentences, each traceable to the register.
The current-state architecture as {client} runs it today, with a caption.
The logical architecture hypothesis, clearly labelled as a hypothesis, with a caption.
What the hypothesis proposes, component by component, and the evidence behind each part.
The direction for each architectural concern (for example identity, observability, data), each with its evidence and confidence.
The minimum every platform should meet at its edges (for example identity, telemetry, lifecycle and data controls), presented as the team's current view for {next_phase} to design.

sections.title: What still needs to be resolved

blocks.guide: One row per open architectural question.

tabs.label: Feasibility Validation
tabs.title: Feasibility Validation
tabs.question: What the feasibility tests proved, what they did not, and what should be tested next.

hero.title: What {phase} proved, and what it did not
hero.lede: The feasibility tests run in {phase}, what each showed, and what should be tested next.

blocks.guide: Two or three sentences on what the tests proved, what they did not, and what that means for the architecture.
One row per test. Write results as [ok] Proven, [warn] Partially proven or [bad] Not proven.
The findings that cut across tests.
How results were scored and what each result label means.
Each test in turn: objective, set-up, result and what it means.
The tests {next_phase} should run next, in priority order.

tabs.label: {phase} to {next_phase}
tabs.title: {phase} to {next_phase}
tabs.question: What {next_phase} reuses, selects and standardizes, and the decisions it must take.

hero.title: What {next_phase} reuses, selects and standardizes
hero.lede: How {phase} findings translate into the scope of {next_phase}.

blocks.guide: The scope of {next_phase} in a few sentences, and the principle behind it (for example reuse what works, standardize the edges).
One row per capability. Write positions as [ok] Reuse, [info] Select or [warn] Standardize.
One row per decision carried into {next_phase}.

tabs.label: Evidence Base
tabs.title: Evidence Base
tabs.question: The sessions, materials and assumptions behind every finding.

hero.title: Evidence, assumptions and visibility
hero.lede: The sessions, materials and assumptions behind every finding in this hub.

blocks.guide: How evidence was gathered and graded, and where visibility was limited.
One row per session.
One row per document, diagram or repository reviewed.
One row per material assumption.
